chunk_findings.detail: The fallback instruction is the only mechanism by which the agent-supplied summary is supposed to satisfy the "if none landed" check, but it does not ask for the role the lookup uses. The intent states the SessionStart:compact output must ask the agent to write `ddflow session note --role summary`, and that the recorded note carries role `compaction`/`summary`; here the command is `ddflow session note --text "<…>"`, with no `--role`, so the note is stored under whatever the default role is (not `summary`/`compaction`). Consequently, in the scenario the fallback exists for — PreCompact failed/skipped (e.g. `CP.record` raised, or `source: compact` arrives with no prior record) — the agent runs the suggested command, a note is written with the wrong role, `CP.latest(log, session_id)` still returns nothing on the next SessionStart:compact, and the same "No record of what this session was doing reached ddflow" prompt is emitted again forever; the summary never reaches the "## Before this compaction" section it was meant to populate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py `_after_compaction` (the `ddflow session note --text "…"` fallback message)

chunk_findings.detail: The write path resolves an identity — `resolved, _layer = resolve_agent_id(repo, cfg, agent)` followed by `EventLog(repo, resolved, …)` — and stores the compaction note in that agent's log, even computing `held` from `st.items` where `i.lease.holder == resolved`. The read path instead builds `EventLog(repo, log_cfg=Config.load(repo).log)` with no agent at all, so it reads the default agent's log, even though `_session_start(repo, agent, stdin)` already has the agent available to pass down. Whenever `resolve_agent_id` yields anything other than EventLog's default agent (which is precisely what that function exists to honor — an agent-id override/config layer), the PreCompact note lands in one log file and `CP.latest` queries another, returning `""`; the operator then gets the "No record …" fallback on every post-compaction SessionStart and the digest that was successfully recorded is never re-injected. If `EventLog`'s agent parameter has no default, this path raises on every SessionStart:compact and `_session_start` degrades to the `_(compaction record unavailable: …)_` branch, likewise never showing the record.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py `_after_compaction` vs `_record_compaction` (EventLog agent scope)

chunk_findings.detail: The truncation slice `text[-(budget - len(who) - 5):]` assumes `budget - len(who) - 5 >= 1`. When the configured budget is small enough that this expression is `<= 0`, the slice silently inverts/drops the sign and no longer keeps the tail. Concretely, with `cfg.session.compaction_digest_chars = 10` and the newest turn being an assistant message, `who = "agent"` (len 5) so the index is `10 - 5 - 5 = 0` and `text[-0:]` is the *entire* message, not its end: the returned digest is `"agent: ..." + full_text`, i.e. it can be thousands of characters against a 10-character budget. With `budget = 12` and an operator turn, the index is `12 - 8 - 5 = -1`, so `text[-(-1):] == text[1:]` — again nearly the whole message instead of its last ~1 character. So for any `budget <= len(who) + 5` (≤13 for `"operator"`, ≤10 for `"agent"`) the function violates the very bound it exists to enforce, and the documented behaviour ("the last turn alone is over budget: keep its end") is not what happens. The knob is user-settable and the whole point of the feature is a bounded digest, so a low setting silently produces an unbounded note. Guarding with `max(0, ...)`/clamping the budget to at least `len(who) + 6` fixes it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/compaction.py:60 (`digest`, single-over-budget branch)

chunk_findings.detail:
When a compact happens with no previously recorded note, `_after_compaction` emits this instruction to the agent:

    '`ddflow session note --text "<what you were doing, what is next>"`'

but the change's stated contract (part b) is that the SessionStart:compact output asks the agent to write `ddflow session note --role summary`. The command actually advertised omits `--role summary`, so the note the agent writes is not tagged with the summary role that this feature relies on (`_record_compaction` records role `compaction`, and querying is done through `CP.latest(log, session_id)`). Concretely: run a session, let it compact without a PreCompact note, the agent follows the injected line and runs `ddflow session note --text "..."`; if `session note` files that under its default role (not `summary`/`compaction`), the next `SessionStart:compact` still returns the "No record …" branch, so the fallback re-emits itself every compaction and never converges to the intended self-heal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py `_after_compaction` (the fallback branch)

chunk_findings.detail: When the most recent transcript turn is the only candidate and is over budget, the truncation is `text[-(budget - len(who) - 5):]`. The slice stop expression is only a positive "keep the last N chars" when `budget > len(who) + 5` (`len(who)` is 8 for `"operator"`, 5 for `"agent"`). For any configured `compaction_digest_chars` at or below that threshold the bound is violated: with `budget == len(who) + 5` the expression is `text[-0:]`, i.e. `text[0:]`, so the *entire* (whitespace-collapsed) turn is embedded; with a smaller budget, e.g. `budget == 10` and `who == "operator"`, it becomes `text[3:]`, which drops 3 characters off the front and keeps everything else. Input: `cfg.session.compaction_digest_chars = 13` and a transcript whose last user entry is a 5 000-character message → `record` stores a note far larger than the configured digest budget, defeating the "bounded digest" guarantee the knob is supposed to provide (redaction still applies, so this is a size/contract bug, not a secret leak).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/compaction.py:65 (`digest` truncation slice)
